From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: KitchenCo discovery: observability + evals — recap & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the walkthrough of the two main product flows (Recipes and Delivery Summaries) and the specific incidents you called out. Quick recap of what we heard, success criteria you mentioned, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points we captured
- Regression detection is slow: you only find model quality regressions after customer reports, not automatically.
- No consistent golden prompt set: teams run ad-hoc prompt tests across services.
- Limited tracing & per-route visibility: hard to map a bad response back to route/version/inputs.
- Cost and per-token visibility: hard to attribute spend to product features.

Success criteria (what KitchenCo wants to see within 8–12 weeks)
- Automated regression alerts on quality metrics (e.g., hallucination/incorrect-entity rate) with <24h detection for 3%+ regressions.
- Per-route dashboards (latency p50/p95, cost, error rate) and tracing hooks to link tokens to request context.
- Golden prompt suite for core intents with periodic evals and A/B rollout guardrails.

What Redwood can deliver quickly
- Dashboards: standard observability board template (latency, cost, hallucination metrics, embedding drift).
- Tracing hooks: small SDK changes to propagate request metadata and sampling to your infra.
- Evals/golden prompts: help assemble a starter set, run baseline evals, surface regressions by route.

Immediate next steps
1) Marcus to run a 45-min technical deep-dive with your engineering team to map tracing integration and sampling points (proposed: Thu 8/13 10am PDT).
2) Sarah/Tom: share a sample prompt set + 1 week of anonymized traces (request attached) so we can scope dashboard panels and eval baselines.
3) Redwood to deliver a one-page action plan + timeline (attached) and a draft SOW for procurement.

Attachments: kitchenco_discussion_notes.txt (meeting notes).

If this aligns, I’ll lock the Marcus/Dev time and send calendar invites.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Following Kimberly’s recap and Sarah’s sample prompts, I sketched a technical checklist to cover what we discussed. High level items and minimal implementation notes below; I’ll bring more concrete code snippets in the tech deep-dive.

1) Tracing hooks (priority)
- SDK shim to propagate route_id, model_version, prompt_hash, and sampling_id.
- Server-side collection: store traces as JSON lines; include token-level timestamps to compute p50/p95 generation times.
- Attach trace_hooks_spec.pdf with proposed header names and sampling rates.

2) Dashboards (observability)
- Per-route panels: latency (p50/p95), tokens-per-response, cost-per-route, error/hallucination rate (derived).
- Evals dashboard: baseline pass/fail rate for golden prompts, trend lines, and regression annotations.

3) Golden prompts & evals
- Start with a 200-item golden set covering core intents.
- Daily headless evals + weekly human spot-checks.
- Regression alerting on >3% drop vs baseline over a 48h window.

4) Rollout guardrails
- Canary policy: 5% of traffic, health checks for latency and hallucination metric; automatic rollback on regression or lat p95 spike >20%.

5) Security/compliance notes
- We’ll need a sanitized trace export and list of endpoints that call external models for SOC2 evidence.

Action items
- Kimberly: confirm tech session time (Thu 8/13 10am PDT proposed).
- Sarah: share sample traces and confirm who on your eng team will join.
- Dev: I’ll loop you for compliance questions and SSO/roles.

Attachments: trace_hooks_spec.pdf

—Marcus
